headlines.title: Philip Morris vs. British American Tobacco: Which Tobacco Dividend Is Better for Retirees?
headlines.summary: One tobacco giant pays a fatter check today, while the other keeps raising its payout year after year. For retirees counting on income through decades of living expenses, the bigger yield may hide a trap worth examining before you buy.

headlines.title: Higher Rates Are Testing Philip Morris Stock and Other Dividend Defensives
headlines.summary: Fed officials are again talking tough on inflation, and markets are taking them at their word. Higher for longer rates can punish richly priced growth stories, yet often leave more defensive, dividend-paying value stocks coming under fresh scrutiny from investors hunting for resilience and income. This article examines what that shift may mean and walks through three stocks exposed to this latest Fed rhetoric from our higher-rate-focused screener.

headlines.title: A $5.2 Billion Fund Dumps These 3 Stocks
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysIlex Capital Partners, a fund with $5. 15 billion of US stocks, sold its whole stakes in Keurig Dr Pepper, Yum! Brands and Philip Morris International in the third quarter, its 13F shows.

headlines.title: How Many Shares of Altria or Philip Morris Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends?
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAt today’s prices, about 2,703 shares of Altria, or roughly $210,600, pay $1,000 a month in dividends. Philip Morris International takes about 1,875 shares, or roughly $368,700.

description: Philip Morris International Inc. operates as a tobacco company. The company offers cigarettes and smoke-free products, including heat-not-burn, e-vapor, and oral nicotine products under the IQOS, VEEV, and ZYN brands; and consumer accessories, such as lighters and matches. It also offers wellness products. The company was incorporated in 1987 and is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.
